reviews.comment: Class I look back on and laugh about now. Lectures and material will definitely be most conceptually difficult of all your classes. However, he is an amazing professor, very intelligent, easy to reach, and super willing to help. Cannot exaggerate how bad he wants you to succeed. Grading also more than makes up for difficulty. Should be easy A.

Course materials are definitely very difficult, especially for freshmen who tend to be taking this course. However, he grades the course very leniently which more than adequately makes up for the added difficulty of being an honors course.

The class is pretty advanced, and goes into topics such as quantum mechanics. He is a research professor with a specialty in P-Chem, so a lot of the topics he will go into are P-Chem adjacent. That being said, this was one of the most intellectually stimulating classes I took this semester. It's not an easy A, but it is very doable to make an A.

Professor Tabor's honors gen-chem was so far removed from a general chemistry course that we couldn't help other non-honors students with their homework. We covered quantum and psychical chemistry material without knowing the basics, so exams were heavily curved when the entire class failed. Our grades were good, but our understanding was not.

He's a pretty helpful guy, and he's very enthusiastic. That being said, HIS CLASS IS PAINFUL. He teaches concepts that require an extremely advanced understanding of calculus, physics (classical and quantum), and sometimes chemistry. For all intents and purposes, this class has a prerequisite of calc 3, physics 207, and chem 119.

Tabor was a very forgiving grader on exams, and gave lots of extra credit opportunities. However, he is not a good teacher for beginners chemistry. He doesn't explain much freshman chemistry, and generally expects you to know most of it already. This is not good because his class is supposed to be the intro to chem class. Be prepared to stress.

The lectures covered very challenging material not taught in AP Chem. However, exams were graded leniently and each had 20 bonus points, and an 83+ in the class was an A, so despite the difficult content it was easy to get an A by doing the homework and going to class. Tabor is very enthusiastic about the content and very willing to help students.

Dr. Tabor is scarily in love with chemistry! Don't take this class if you haven't taken AP Chemistry and/or don't have a basic understanding of physics + calculus. While they're not on the tests, its required to understand lecture, which often devolves into random derivations of equations. The curve (83 = A) will make sure most people make an A/B.

I didn't take AP Chem, but even those who did found this class really hard. Tabor is kind and clearly passionate, but his content is just so theoretical and difficult to understand. It's nothing like the normal CHEM119 sections. He does grade lightly, but be prepared to study A LOT. Tests are all FRQ with lots of partial credit and ~120 points.

Material could be challenging but exams are graded lightly so you can get partial credit for writing something that's even slightly on the right track. There are 20 freebie points on exams so you can score over 100. Dr. Tabor was enthusiastic in his lectures, did his best to help us understand difficult material. Not an overwhelming class, A is 83+

This class is very stressful in the beginning because the rigor of work seems intense, but after the first exam it becomes quite clear that as long you do not snort glue you will pass this class. A basic level of chemistry and physics could easily get you a B minimum in the course, without any further studying. Homework was the worst part.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tabor is a very passionate and kind professor. He is accessible outside of class and encourages visits during his office hours. The class is challenging and will require a lot of critical thinking. However, Dr. Tabor rewards effort as long as you try. Take this class if you have a passion for chemistry and actually enjoy learning.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: In my class specifically, an 83 was an A so that was really nice. I will say that his tests are very difficult but he knows that so grades very lightly. This class requires a lot of studying but if you are on the right track on the test you will get the most points. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

From the first class to the last Dr. Tabor's passionate love of science was on clear display. I could always count on his lectures being logical and able to used to study from. He is a kind grader, an approachable person to discuss problems with, and gives some of the hardest tests I have ever taken. Expect to read, learn math, and learn more math.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Tabor is always available even you cannot go to the office hour. The lecture is very clear. Some hard concepts are explained in a very easy way. Definitely will recommend it if you are new to Statistical Mechanics.

This was a really difficult course, simply due to the material, but Dr. Tabor was very passionate and made his lectures easy to follow. He was really great about offering time outside of class and feedback. All of his homework furthered my understanding of the class, and did not feel like busy work. He offered extra credit for every problem set.

Need significant understanding of chemistry/physics(2+ years)/calculus. He is very nice & obviously passionate, but material is nearly impossible w/o the chemistry foundation that we came to this class for. NO tutoring or SI sessions available for the honors section. Class was just too intense for gen chem. Grades fast, very accessible via slack.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Tabor is very passionate about all things chemistry. The class is very difficult, however he is a very fast grader, offers great feedback, and is available outside of class. The exams are very difficult because you don't know what to expect. Honestly, I didn't read the textbook and still got an A solely because of Dr. Tabor and his grading.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class and liked Dr. Tabor's teaching style, which is lecture and textbook-based, but this was very much an honors-level course. I found reading the textbook and taking notes over it to be helpful if time-consuming, as was going to office hours. Be prepared to put in the work to understand the content, even with an AP background.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Tabor is very passionate about teaching this class. Although it is a freshman level course, it does require background knowledge in chemistry and physics. I enjoy attending lecture, and reading the textbook helps understand concepts a lot better. If you don't skip class, read the textbook, and attend office hours, an A is achievable.

Tabor is very passionate about chem and it is evident he is good at what he does but the content isn't explained well IMO on a fundamental level (I do not have a PhD in chem or phys). Strong physics, calculus, and chemistry background are needed. AP CHEM IS NOT ENOUGH. The grades are given back quickly though and he is available outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Tabor is very passionate and enjoys teaching the class. The concepts could be explained better. Definitely dont recommend taking unless you did Calc, physics, and chem in high school. There is extra credit and is weighted to where the majority of the class will get As. Recommend doing multimedia questions for the tests (helps a lot).

Dr. Tabor is very passionate about his work but this shouldnt be a Freshman level class. His material is hard and doesnt prepare you for future classes. Ive tried to come to him with concerns over how I am struggling and he didnt do much to help me. The lectures are all spent on deriving equations and its info that you dont need for the test.
Great person and loves what he's teaching but too difficult for a general freshman chemistry class. Do not take this class if you haven't taken calculus, AP chemistry. and AP physics.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just don't do it. This class alone took up over half my time. He is a fine person, but you won't learn the fundamentals and will instead use all your time trying to understand how to mathematically derive quantum mechanics (Not on the test!?!). People are seriously planning on retaking this course despite passing it just to be ready for chem 120.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Tabor is very passionate about the class and gives great feedback. He also grades pretty tough. If you haven't taken chemistry, physics, and calculus in the high school or college level I wouldn't take the class. Half the lectures are spent with him deriving complex equations from other equally complex equations. Hit heavily on quantum.
